headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while whales quietly walk coins off exchanges, but bitcoin's own ETF tape just broke the streak
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs. That's five of seven majors in a technical uptrend structure, with the two laggards being the two furthest from their 12-month highs (DOGE -71.2%, ADA -78.8%). Bitcoin itself is up 1.4% on the day, up a much quieter 0.5% on the week, and up 21.8% on the month, three windows that don't agree on urgency even if they agree on direction. ETH shows the same tension in sharper relief: up 2.1% today, down 1.9% on the week, up 31.9% on the month. That's a market where the monthly trend is doing the heavy lifting and the daily print is just noise riding on top of it.

Momentum is where the first real divergence shows up. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 71, ETH at 69, SOL at 69.1, all technically overbought by the classic 70 threshold, and all still MACD-bullish (MACD above signal). That's a trend accelerating, not resting, at least for now. XRP and BNB sit in the low-to-mid 60s, still constructive but with more room before overbought. DOGE and ADA are the odd ones out, both below their 200-day lines, both MACD-bearish, both with RSI near 50 to 55, which reads as trend-negative but momentum-neutral rather than trend-negative and falling. Worth naming: XRP and ADA and DOGE all show a weekly decline (-5.0%, -13.8%, -9.1% respectively) sitting underneath a positive monthly number. The week is where the froth is coming out; the month is where the trend still lives.

Positioning adds some texture to that overbought read. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0059% per 8 hours (6.4% annualized), not expensive money to be long. ETH funding is even cheaper at 4.7% annualized. SOL funding is actually negative (-0.4% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual state for an asset up 35.4% on the month with RSI at 69. That's crowded-but-cheap, not crowded-and-expensive, and it matters: elevated RSI paired with low or negative funding is a different fragility profile than elevated RSI paired with funding running hot. Long/short account ratios lean long across the board (BTC 1.10, ETH 1.23, SOL 1.80, XRP 2.47, DOGE 4.00), so retail leverage is skewed long even where funding isn't punishing it yet. BTC open interest sits at $2.16B on this venue with liquidations over roughly 23 hours split $8.2M longs versus $7.0M shorts, a mild long-side flush, not a cascade.

Flows are the most interesting board today because they disagree with each other inside the same asset. BTC ETF flows on 28 Aug posted a $201.9M outflow, but the last five sessions net to a $924.5M inflow, with same_direction_days at just 1, meaning that outflow day was a break from the recent run, not a confirmation of it. ETH ETF flows are cleaner: $102.1M in on 28 Aug, $815.7M net over five sessions, and 10 days running in the same direction, an actual persistent trend by this desk's own bar. Whale exchange flows over the last 72 hours show $176.2M net moving off exchanges in BTC, continuing a pattern visible across the last four tracked weeks (week ending Aug 10 through Aug 31), every one of which shows net value moving onto exchanges in the weekly series, yet the most recent 72-hour window flips to net outflow. Read that carefully: the multi-week trend has been coins moving onto exchanges, and the most recent snapshot shows the opposite. Stablecoin float is up 1.31% over 30 days to $309.6B, which is dry powder sitting on the sideline growing slowly, not surging.

Sentiment reads Greed at 62, inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is optimistic but not at an extreme. That roughly matches what the tape shows: real uptrend structure, cheap-to-moderate funding, and a genuine ETF bid in ETH. Where it doesn't match is bitcoin's own ETF picture, where the crowd's greed sits on top of a day that just broke a positive flow streak, and the whale data, where four weeks of coins moving onto exchanges just gave way to one 72-hour window of coins moving off. Neither is a reversal yet; both are worth tracking rather than trusting on one print.

What to watch: whether BTC's next ETF session confirms the Aug 28 outflow as a pattern or reverts to the five-session inflow trend; whether the 72-hour whale outflow extends into a weekly print that finally breaks the onto-exchanges streak seen every week from Aug 10 through Aug 31; and whether SOL's negative funding flips positive as its RSI sits at 69, since that would mark leverage catching up to price rather than lagging it.
